deploy-bot: [CI] microbench regression alert for PR #7150 — kernel-selection-crossover test shows +9.8% p99 latency vs baseline (threshold 5%).

alisa: ugh, saw that in the dashboard. CI details?

ben: link to CI run: https://ci.redwood/7150/compare — microbench logs show the delta happens in kernel_selector.cpp:choose_kernel() path.

carmen: quick summary from the bench: small-batch token streams (batch_size <= 4) with median seq_len 64 regress, larger batches unaffected. looks like we switched the crossover point where we pick fused-attn vs chunked-attn.

dmitri: repro locally with the perf harness: `./bench micro --profile kernel-crossover --runs 100 --batch 2 --seq 64` => p99 shifted from 12.3ms -> 13.5ms. I captured a flamegraph.

eva: can you paste the flamegraph top functions?

dmitri: top is kernel_dispatcher::dispatch -> fused_attn::run -> fallback_chunked::run (extra copy path). there's an extra memcpy introduced in the new selection path.

alisa: which commit touched the selector? blame points to 3a9f2b9 (PR 7128) — heuristic refactor 'prefer_chunked_on_memory_pressure' with a new 'crossover_length' calc.

ben: running git bisect across the CI artifacts. preliminary bisect points to commit 3a9f2b9 indeed.

carmen: patch snippet in 3a9f2b9 changed the condition from `if (seq_len > crossover_len)` to `if (seq_len >= crossover_len)` and added a path that forces chunked for borderline cases.

alisa: that off-by-one can move a lot of requests across kernels for seq 64 if our crossover_len was 64. we probably flipped many microbench cases.

dmitri: here's the log segment from CI: ```
kernel chosen: fused_attn (seq=63)
kernel chosen: chunked_attn (seq=64)  // new behavior
copy bytes: 8192 -> 12288  // extra memcpy in chunked path
```

eva: is the memcpy avoidable? maybe we can reuse the kv buffer or do an in-place transform.

carmen: short-term I propose reverting the >= change to > so we don't flip borderline cases. it's a tiny behavioral revert and should pass perf thresholds.

ben: agreed. but PR 7128 also included logic for memory-pressure hint. we should make the revert surgical: only roll back the >= change and add unit tests for both sides.

alisa: also add a microbench for seq_len == crossover_len to catch this. Add an assertion in kernel_selector unit tests that selection is deterministic for equal case.

dmitri: I'll open PR 7151 (hotfix) that reverts the operator and adds tests + perf harness entry. planning to run CI with the hotfix now.

eva: ping me when CI completes, I'll review the flamegraphs and verify no regressions on other batch sizes.

deploy-bot: CI run queued for PR 7151. Estimated completion ~12m.

ben: one more action: add telemetry metric for 'selected_kernel' per (model, seq_bucket, batch_bucket) so we can detect sharp switches on rollout.

carmen: yes please — that would have surfaced this earlier in canary.

alisa: assigned dmitri to PR 7151, ben to the telemetry task, carmen to add microbench test vectors. eva will validate graphs post-CI.

dmitri: quick note for the postmortem: mention that a subtle >= change moved a large mass of real requests across a kernel boundary which exposed a copy in the chunked path — we should consider perf-sensitivity reviews for kernel-selection changes.

eva: thanks team. If the hotfix passes, let's schedule a cautious rollout and watch the telemetry for 24h. :eyes:

deploy-bot: CI for PR 7151 succeeded (build+microbench). perf diff: baseline vs hotfix: -0.2% p99 (within noise).

alisa: great, merging hotfix and rolling out canary to dedicated pool A.

ben: created tracking ticket RW-4312 for telemetry + canary dashboard.

carmen: will follow up with a short blameless post in #eng-runtime summarizing root cause and mitigation.

alisa: thanks everyone. closing thread once canary is stable. :thumbsup:
